Isotropic Grassmann bundles imply smooth rank strata and reduced-geometric irreducibility. The supplied complete finite checks agree but are not used to infer the universal result.

originality.rationale: The 2023 general Leibniz Nijenhuis paper contains structural definitions, deformation/cohomology theory and examples but no classification of all Heisenberg Nijenhuis operators, isotropic image normal forms, or q-enumeration. The 2024 regular-semisimple three-dimensional Lie Nijenhuis paper explicitly excludes regular semisimple structures on nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebras and supplies only special examples, so it neither states nor implies the nonregular all-dimensional census. The 2025 real three-dimensional Leibniz tables and 2023/2026 pre-Lie/associative work do not dominate the Lie all-fields claim. Closest published Heisenberg research records concern automorphisms or subgroup/subalgebra commutativity, not the operator locus. Equivalence under alternate terminology remains a concrete risk.
residual_risks: Equivalent classification may exist under hereditary/symplectic operators, torsion-zero matrices, or Hamiltonian terminology without Nijenhuis in the title.
Search coverage does not establish global novelty or independently verify unpublished work.
The 2025 real Leibniz paper and 2024 complex semisimple paper do not address finite-field rank counts, but special cases in other algebra literature may coincide.
The geometric statement concerns the reduced variety; no scheme-theoretic smoothness of the full Nijenhuis equation scheme is asserted.
